title: Search 2D Matrix
contract: Rows are sorted and each row's first value exceeds the previous row's last. Return whether target exists in a nonempty rectangular matrix.
brute: for(int r=0;r<a.length;r++)for(int c=0;c<a[0].length;c++){emit("Inspect a cell","cell",new int[]{r,c},"value",a[r][c]);if(a[r][c]==target)return true;}return false;
optimal: int cols=a[0].length,lo=0,hi=a.length*cols-1;while(lo<=hi){int mid=lo+(hi-lo)/2,value=a[mid/cols][mid%cols];emit("Binary-search the flattened order","range",new int[]{lo,mid,hi},"cell",new int[]{mid/cols,mid%cols},"value",value);if(value==target)return true;if(value<target)lo=mid+1;else hi=mid-1;}return false;
reasoning: Scan each cell without exploiting ordering.
The row-boundary condition makes the flattened matrix globally sorted.
Map flat index to row=index/columns and column=index%columns. Matrices with only independently sorted rows and columns need a different staircase search; the stronger contract matters.
